subproblem.title: The determinant n-covector of ℝⁿ: every n-covector is α(e)·ε, and ε = ±1 on orthonormal bases
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), and let e = (e₁, …, eₙ) = ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) be the standard orthonormal basis. There is an n-covector ε ∈ Covector (Euclid n) n (a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝⁿ) with three properties. (i) ε(e) = 1. (ii) α(v) = ε(v)·α(e) for every n-covector α and every v : Fin n → ℝⁿ. (iii) ε(τ) = 1 or ε(τ) = −1 for every orthonormal family τ : Fin n → ℝⁿ whose span is ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ ε : Covector (Euclid n) n, ε ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) = 1 ∧ (∀ (α : Covector (Euclid n) n) (v : Fin n → Euclid n), α v = ε v * α ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)) ∧ ∀ τ : Fin n → Euclid n, Orthonormal ℝ τ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = ⊤ → ε τ = 1 ∨ ε τ = -1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the notation paragraph, step 2 and the determinant part of step 3 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_cz_top_density (the density part of the Constancy Theorem, Simon Ch. 6, 2.34), with all details filled in. No sibling is used.
Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). An n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid n) n = Euclid n [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝⁿ. Let b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ, an orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ indexed by Fin n, and e := ⇑b. Write b.toBasis for the underlying basis; ⇑b.toBasis = ⇑b = e (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis).
1. Let D := b.toBasis.det : Euclid n [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ be the determinant alternating form with respect to b.toBasis. By Module.Basis.det_self, D(e) = 1.
2. D is continuous as a map (Fin n → ℝⁿ) → ℝ.
   - By Module.Basis.det_apply, D(v) = det(b.toBasis.toMatrix v).
   - The (i, j) entry of b.toBasis.toMatrix v is b.toBasis.repr (v j) i (Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply), which equals (b.toBasis.coord i)(v j) (Module.Basis.coord_apply).
   - The coordinate functional b.toBasis.coord i is a linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional), and v ↦ v j is continuous (continuous_apply).
   - So every entry is continuous in v, and the matrix-valued map v ↦ b.toBasis.toMatrix v is continuous (continuous_pi twice).
   - The determinant of a continuous matrix-valued map is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det).
3. Let ε be the continuous alternating map whose underlying alternating map is D and whose continuity is step 2 (in Lean: { D with cont := hcont }). Then ε ∈ Covector (Euclid n) n and ε(v) = D(v) for every v (definitionally). By step 1, ε(e) = 1; this is property (i).
4. Property (ii). Let α be an n-covector and v : Fin n → ℝⁿ. Apply Mathlib's AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det to the basis b.toBasis and to the alternating map α.toAlternatingMap underlying α. It gives α.toAlternatingMap = α(e) • D. Evaluating both sides at v gives α(v) = α(e)·D(v) = ε(v)·α(e).
5. Property (iii). Let τ : Fin n → ℝⁿ be orthonormal with span(range τ) = ⊤.
   - Then ⊤ ≤ span(range τ), so B := OrthonormalBasis.mk hτ (this inequality) is an orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ indexed by Fin n, with ⇑B = τ (OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk).
   - By Mathlib's OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real b B, the change-of-basis determinant between two orthonormal bases of a real inner product space is ±1: b.toBasis.det ⇑B = 1 ∨ b.toBasis.det ⇑B = −1.
   - That is, D(τ) = 1 ∨ D(τ) = −1, i.e. ε(τ) = 1 ∨ ε(τ) = −1.
6. Steps 3–5 show that ε has the three required properties. ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_top_density_det_covector_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_top_density_det_covector_aux). The candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean, and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge.
proof_key_steps: Let D := b.toBasis.det for b = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ. Then D(e) = 1 (Module.Basis.det_self).
D is continuous: D(v) = det(b.toBasis.toMatrix v) (det_apply), the coordinates are continuous, and Continuous.matrix_det applies. So ε := { D with cont } is an n-covector with ε(e) = 1.
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det gives α = α(e)•D, hence α(v) = ε(v)·α(e) for all α and v.
An orthonormal τ spanning ⊤ gives B := OrthonormalBasis.mk with ⇑B = τ. Then det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real gives ε(τ) = D(τ) = ±1.

subproblem.title: An IM representation in ℝⁿ oriented by σ·(e₁∧⋯∧eₙ) acts by an integer L¹_loc density
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝⁿ = Euclid n be open, and let R : IMRep V n with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult and ξ = R.orient. Let Hⁿ = μHE[n] and e = ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ). Let σ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be measurable such that, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y, σ(y) ∈ {1, −1} and ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)·α(e) for every n-covector α. Then there is g : ℝⁿ → ℤ with two properties. First, y ↦ (g(y) : ℝ) is locally Lebesgue-integrable on V (LocallyIntegrableOn … V volume). Second, R.action ω = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g(y)·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every n-form ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n, not necessarily smooth or compactly supported. Here R.action ω = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)) (R : IMRep V n) (σ : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen V → Measurable σ → (∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), (σ y = 1 ∨ σ y = -1) ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid n) n, R.orient y α = σ y * α ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)) → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℤ, LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n, R.action ω = ∫ y, (g y : ℝ) * ω y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–7 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_cz_top_density, with all details filled in; the measurable σ̃ there is the given measurable σ here. No sibling is used.
Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n, Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ := volume on Euclid n, e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ). For R : IMRep V n write M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult : ℝⁿ → ℕ and ξ := R.orient. The IMRep fields used are:
   - measurableSet_carrier: M is measurable;
   - measurable_mult: θ is measurable;
   - locallyIntegrable_mult: ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V.
By definition (IMRep.action), R.action ω = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y). Mathlib's EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n gives Hⁿ = Lⁿ on Euclid n.
1. Define g : ℝⁿ → ℤ by
   - g(y) := θ(y) if y ∈ M and 0 ≤ σ(y);
   - g(y) := −θ(y) if y ∈ M and σ(y) < 0;
   - g(y) := 0 if y ∉ M.
2. Measurability. g is a nested if-then-else over the measurable sets M and {y | 0 ≤ σ(y)} (measurableSet_le, since σ is measurable). Its branches y ↦ (θ(y) : ℤ), y ↦ −(θ(y) : ℤ) and the constant 0 are measurable: θ is measurable, every map out of ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_top), and Measurable.neg handles the sign. Hence g is measurable (Measurable.ite). So is y ↦ (g(y) : ℝ), since every map out of ℤ is measurable (measurable_from_top). In particular it is AEStronglyMeasurable for every measure.
3. Pointwise facts.
   (a) For every y, ‖(g(y) : ℝ)‖ₑ ≤ 1_M(y)·θ(y), i.e. ≤ M.indicator (fun y => (θ y : ℝ≥0∞)) y. If y ∈ M then |g(y)| = θ(y); if y ∉ M then g(y) = 0.
   (b) g(y) = 0 for y ∉ M, hence g(y)·ω(y)(e) = 0 for every y ∉ M and every n-form ω.
4. Local integrability. V is open, hence locally closed (IsOpen.isLocallyClosed), and ℝⁿ is locally compact. So by locallyIntegrableOn_iff it suffices to show that y ↦ (g(y) : ℝ) is Lⁿ-integrable on every compact K ⊆ V.
   - Measurability is step 2.
   - Finiteness: ∫⁻_K ‖g‖ₑ dLⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_K 1_M·θ dLⁿ (lintegral_mono with 3(a)).
   - This equals ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dLⁿ (lintegral_indicator, M measurable, then Measure.restrict_restrict).
   - This equals ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ (Hⁿ = Lⁿ), which is < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult K.
Hence IntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) K volume for every compact K ⊆ V, i.e. LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume.
5. A.e. identity. Let ω be any n-form. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y we have y ∈ M (ae_restrict_mem, M measurable). Applying the hypothesis with α = ω(y) gives σ(y) ∈ {1, −1} and ξ(y)(ω(y)) = σ(y)·ω(y)(e).
   - If σ(y) = 1, then 0 ≤ σ(y), so g(y) = θ(y) and θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) = θ(y)·ω(y)(e) = g(y)·ω(y)(e).
   - If σ(y) = −1, then σ(y) < 0, so g(y) = −θ(y) and θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) = −θ(y)·ω(y)(e) = g(y)·ω(y)(e).
Hence θ·ξ(ω) = g·ω(e) holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.
6. Formula.
   - By step 5 and integral_congr_ae for Hⁿ⌞M (no integrability is needed): R.action ω = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_M g·ω(e) dHⁿ.
   - By 3(b) and setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (no integrability is needed): ∫_M g·ω(e) dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g·ω(e) dHⁿ.
   - Since Hⁿ = Lⁿ: R.action ω = ∫ g(y)·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y).
7. Steps 4 and 6 prove the statement with this g. ∎
Implementation notes (not part of the proof): (1) To use setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero right to left in Lean, first rewrite volume as μHE[n]. Then pass the lemma the explicit vanishing hypothesis 3(b) for the integrand y ↦ (g y : ℝ) * ω y e. That way the rewrite acts on the right-hand integral and not on the left-hand set integral, which is itself an integral for the restricted measure. (2) Name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_top_density_of_sign_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_top_density_of_sign_aux). The candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean, and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge.
proof_key_steps: Define g := θ on M∩{σ ≥ 0}, −θ on M∩{σ < 0}, and 0 off M. Then g is measurable (Measurable.ite), |g| ≤ θ·1_M, and g = 0 off M.
For compact K ⊆ V: ∫⁻_K |g| dLⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞, using lintegral_indicator, restrict_restrict and Hⁿ = Lⁿ. So g is locally integrable on V by locallyIntegrableOn_iff (V is open).
θ·ξ(ω) = g·ω(e) Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., because σ = ±1 and ξ = σ·e a.e.
R.action ω = ∫_M g·ω(e) dHⁿ = ∫ g·ω(e) dHⁿ = ∫ g·ω(e) dLⁿ, by integral_congr_ae, setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero and Hⁿ = Lⁿ. No integrability is needed.

The supplied piecewise integer density is measurable, its norm bound gives compact-set integrability using locallyIntegrable_mult and Hausdorff-volume equality, and openness yields local integrability. The almost-everywhere integrand identity and vanishing outside the carrier prove the formula without additional integrability assumptions. The proof uses no sibling conclusion.

subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)) (R : IMRep V n), ∃ σ : Euclid n → ℝ, Measurable σ ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), (σ y = 1 ∨ σ y = -1) ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid n) n, R.orient y α = σ y * α ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_cz_top_density, with all details filled in; the measurable modification σ̃ of step 4 is produced here. Uses the sibling det_covector (Submission.dtc_bc_cz_top_density_det_covector).
Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n, Hⁿ := μHE[n], e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ). For R : IMRep V n write M := R.carrier and ξ := R.orient : ℝⁿ → MultiVector n n, where MultiVector n n = (Covector (Euclid n) n →L[ℝ] ℝ). The IMRep fields used are:
   - aestronglyMeasurable_orient: ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M;
   - orients: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y there is a subspace Q of ℝⁿ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ y) Q.
No property of V and no positivity of n is used.
1. By det_covector at n, fix ε ∈ Covector (Euclid n) n with:
   (i) ε(e) = 1;
   (ii) α(v) = ε(v)·α(e) for every n-covector α and every v : Fin n → ℝⁿ;
   (iii) ε(τ) = 1 ∨ ε(τ) = −1 for every orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝⁿ with span(range τ) = ⊤.
2. Measurable sign. Define σ₀(y) := ξ(y)(ε).
   - σ₀ is the composition of ξ with the continuous linear map "evaluation at ε", ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ ε : MultiVector n n →L[ℝ] ℝ. So σ₀ is AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable with aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
   - Let σ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk σ₀. Then σ is strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.stronglyMeasurable_mk), hence measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurable).
   - Moreover σ₀ = σ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk).
3. It remains to prove that for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y, σ(y) ∈ {1, −1} and ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)·α(e) for every n-covector α. The intersection of two Hⁿ⌞M-conull sets is conull, so it suffices to prove this at every y where the orients property holds and σ₀(y) = σ(y). Fix such a y.
4. The tangent space is all of ℝⁿ. Choose Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ y) Q. By HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq, finrank Q = n. Also finrank ℝⁿ = card (Fin n) = n (finrank_euclideanSpace, Fintype.card_fin). Hence Q = ⊤ (Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq).
5. By IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ y) Q, choose τ : Fin n → ℝⁿ orthonormal with span(range τ) = Q = ⊤ such that either
   (a) ξ(y)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or
   (b) ξ(y)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
By (iii), ε(τ) = 1 ∨ ε(τ) = −1. By (ii), α(τ) = ε(τ)·α(e) for every α.
6. In case (a) put s := ε(τ); in case (b) put s := −ε(τ). In both cases s = 1 ∨ s = −1 by step 5, and ξ(y)(α) = s·α(e) for every α:
   - in case (a), ξ(y)(α) = α(τ) = ε(τ)·α(e);
   - in case (b), ξ(y)(α) = −α(τ) = −ε(τ)·α(e).
7. Take α = ε in step 6 and use (i): σ₀(y) = ξ(y)(ε) = s·ε(e) = s. Hence σ(y) = σ₀(y) = s, so σ(y) = 1 ∨ σ(y) = −1, and ξ(y)(α) = s·α(e) = σ(y)·α(e) for every α. As y was an arbitrary point of an Hⁿ⌞M-conull set, σ is measurable and has the required a.e. properties. ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_top_density_orient_sign_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_top_density_orient_sign_aux). The candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean, and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge.
proof_key_steps: Fix ε from det_covector: ε(e) = 1, α(v) = ε(v)α(e), and ε = ±1 on orthonormal spanning frames.
σ₀ := ξ(·)(ε) is AEStronglyMeasurable because evaluation at ε is continuous linear. Let σ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk σ₀; it is measurable and σ = σ₀ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.
At a.e. y, orients gives Q with an approximate tangent space and a unit orientation. finrank Q = n forces Q = ⊤.
τ is orthonormal, spans ⊤, and ξ(y) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)). Since α(τ) = ε(τ)α(e) and ε(τ) = ±1, ξ(y)(α) = s·α(e) with s = ±1.
s = s·ε(e) = ξ(y)(ε) = σ₀(y) = σ(y), so σ(y) = ±1 and ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)α(e) a.e.

audit.reason: The type exactly states global measurability and a single conull set on which both conclusions hold for every covector. The proof correctly uses det_covector, identifies the tangent subspace with top by finrank, and transfers continuous evaluation to its measurable modification. Intersecting the two conull sets suffices; no uncountable intersection or undeclared dependency is hidden.
